area: The atom map is exempt from the physical line budget that governs the source it accounts for
finding: The governed commit path enforces a 600-line physical budget on touched source files and refuses with ATM_TOUCHED_PHYSICAL_LINE_BUDGET_BLOCKED. That enforcement observably does not reach the atomization ledger: an owner shard well past the threshold was amended and committed in the same operation whose source file was rejected for crossing it. The asymmetry matters because the atom map is not incidental data. It is the record of how the codebase is atomized, it is read to decide extraction boundaries, and it grows monotonically as coverage grows. A ledger that records atomization while being exempt from the discipline it records will eventually become the largest unatomized artifact in the repository, and the day the budget is extended to cover it, every map update becomes unfixable through the governed path — the update needed to shard it would itself be blocked.
expectedBehavior: State it as a rule rather than a threshold: any artifact that serves as the ledger of atomization must be subject to the same physical budget as the source it accounts for, or must carry a validated sharding strategy that keeps each shard within that budget and is enforced by a validator rather than by convention. Budget coverage must be decided by the role an artifact plays, not by its file extension. If generated projections are deliberately exempt because they are derived, that exemption must be explicit and must not extend to the hand-authored shards those projections are built from.
evidenceOrRepro: 2026-08-15, ATM-GOV-0394. Adding 56 lines to packages/cli/src/commands/git-governance/implementation/commit-command.ts took it from 595 to 651 and the governed commit refused with ATM_TOUCHED_PHYSICAL_LINE_BUDGET_BLOCKED (nestedFailure.errorSummary: 'Governed commit blocked because touched source files exceed the physical line budget (600).'). That refusal was correct and produced a genuine atomization: the file was extracted into a router plus two named lifecycle branches plus a purity contract, at 290/231/173/65 lines. In the same delivery, atomic_workbench/atomization-coverage/path-to-atom-map-shards/owner-shard-cli.json was amended from 1168 to 1180 lines and committed without objection. Both files were touched by one governed commit; only the source file was measured.
followUp: Decide the intended coverage rule first, then enforce it: either extend the touched-file budget to atomization ledger shards, or require and validate a sharding strategy for them. Sequencing matters here and should be recorded with the fix — an already-oversized shard must be split before the budget is extended to cover it, or the split itself becomes unreachable through the governed path, which is the same bootstrap circularity recorded in [ATM-BUG-2026-08-13-013]. Do not write the remedy against a specific shard or a specific line count; the subject is the class of artifacts that account for atomization.
